studies.title: A substrate-specific mTORC1 pathway underlies Birt-Hogg-Dubé syndrome.
studies.finding: A substrate-specific mTORC1-TFEB pathway (RagC/D-dependent) drives Birt-Hogg-Dube kidney disease.

studies.title: G3BPs tether the TSC complex to lysosomes and suppress mTORC1 signaling
studies.finding: Adds a physical brake upstream of mTORC1. G3BP1 and G3BP2, known until then as core stress-granule proteins, also sit on the cytoplasmic face of the lysosome and are what holds the TSC complex there; without them TSC cannot reach its target and mTORC1 becomes over-responsive to amino acids and insulin. studies.title: ER-Lysosome Cholesterol Exchange Regulates Lysosomal Motility Through mTOR-Dependent LAMTOR1 Phosphorylation
studies.finding: Identifies a new layer of control over mTORC1's lysosomal machinery: cholesterol exchange between the ER and lysosome regulates lysosome movement via mTOR-dependent phosphorylation of LAMTOR1, a core component of the Ragulator complex that anchors the Rag GTPases already in this Atlas.

studies.title: Structure of the lysosomal mTORC1-TFEB-Rag-Ragulator megacomplex
studies.finding: First structural view of how mTORC1 actually reaches TFEB to phosphorylate it: two full Rag-Ragulator complexes present a single TFEB molecule to the mTOR active site, one in the normal Raptor-docking arrangement and a second, non-canonical one that grips TFEB's own first helix. studies.title: Forsythoside A Alleviates Hypertensive Nephropathy by Promoting Mitophagy and Inhibiting Ferroptosis via ASCL1-CCNB1/mTOR Pathway.
studies.finding: Forsythoside A binds ASCL1 and blocks the downstream CCNB1/mTOR axis, promoting mitophagy and suppressing ferroptosis to protect against Ang II-induced hypertensive nephropathy in mice — without lowering blood pressure.

studies.title: mTOR controls mitochondrial oxidative function through a YY1-PGC-1alpha transcriptional complex
studies.finding: Showed mTOR isn't just about building proteins - it also runs the cell's POWER plants. mTORC1 drives mitochondrial gene expression and oxygen consumption through a YY1-PGC-1alpha transcriptional program; block mTOR with rapamycin and mitochondrial output falls. Explains part of why mTOR inhibition reshapes metabolism.

studies.title: mTORC1 inhibition upregulates CD20 and enhances anti-CD20 antibody efficacy in B-cell precursor acute lymphoblastic leukemia
studies.finding: mTORC1 inhibitors upregulate CD20 via the AKT-FOXO1 axis and promote B-lineage maturation in B-cell precursor ALL, enhancing the antitumor efficacy of anti-CD20 monoclonal antibodies -- including in high-risk IKZF1-deleted disease -- providing a rationale for combining mTORC1 inhibition with CD20-directed immunotherapy.

studies.title: TOR signaling and rapamycin influence longevity by regulating SKN-1/Nrf and DAF-16/FoxO
studies.finding: In C. elegans, genetic TORC1 inhibition extends lifespan through SKN-1/Nrf and DAF-16/FoxO, whereas rapamycin's lifespan effect requires SKN-1 but not DAF-16, apparently because it also hits TORC2.

studies.title: Ulk1-mediated phosphorylation of AMPK constitutes a negative regulatory feedback loop
studies.finding: ULK1 phosphorylates and inhibits AMPK in return, showing autophagy signaling is a bidirectional feedback loop, not a one-way switch.

studies.title: Recurrent reversible mutations at gaf1 driving metastable TORC1 inhibitor resistance in fission yeast.
studies.finding: Metastable resistance to TORC1 inhibitors (rapamycin plus caffeine) in fission yeast is driven by recurrent, spontaneously reversible loss-of-function mutations in gaf1, a GATA transcription factor and negative growth regulator downstream of TORC1 - a genetic (not epigenetic) toggle that can silently contaminate lab yeast stocks.

studies.title: The kinase mTOR regulates the differentiation of helper T cells through the selective activation of signaling by mTORC1 and mTORC2
studies.finding: mTORC1 and mTORC2 selectively program distinct CD4 helper T-cell lineages.

studies.title: The mTOR kinase differentially regulates effector and regulatory T cell lineage commitment
studies.finding: T cells lacking mTOR fail to become normal effector cells and default toward regulatory T cells, showing mTOR is a master switch for immune cell fate.

studies.title: Rapamycin decelerates cellular senescence
studies.finding: Blagosklonny's key experiment behind his 'hyperfunction' theory of aging. When a cell's division is blocked but mTOR keeps driving growth, the cell tips into permanent senescence. Rapamycin uncouples the two - keeping arrested cells reversible instead of senescent. Direct evidence that mTOR actively drives the senescent state, not just passively accompanies it.

studies.title: IDH3 regulates citrate homeostasis to control metabolic fitness and venetoclax resistance of AML stem cells
studies.finding: IDH3A loss in AML leukemic stem cells reduces TCA cycle flux and raises intracellular citrate, activating AMPK and suppressing mTORC1 (lowering translation), which sensitizes cells to BCL2 inhibition by venetoclax - nominating the IDH3A-citrate-AMPK-mTORC1 axis as a target to overcome venetoclax/azacitidine resistance.

studies.title: Mammalian TOR: a homeostatic ATP sensor
studies.finding: The authors tested whether mTOR signalling responds to the cell's energy level, not only to amino acids. They reported that lowering intracellular ATP reduced signalling through the mTOR pathway, and that this happened independently of amino acid levels. studies.title: mTOR complex 2 is required for the development of prostate cancer induced by Pten loss in mice
studies.finding: mTORC2 is required for prostate cancer driven by Pten loss in mice.

studies.title: Rapamycin-induced insulin resistance is mediated by mTORC2 loss and uncoupled from longevity
studies.finding: Chronic rapamycin (about 2 mg/kg a day, close to the lifespan-extending dose) made mice glucose intolerant and insulin resistant. A clamp test placed the problem in the liver, which kept making glucose, while muscle and fat took up glucose normally. Removing mTORC1 from the liver did not cause this. studies.title: Spalt-related is an inhibitor of mTORC1-mediated growth activated by the integrated stress response
studies.finding: Transcription factor Spalt-related (Salr) is a novel mTORC1 inhibitor in Drosophila activated by the integrated stress response, restricting anabolic growth and lipid storage during nutrient stress. Salr responds to a distinct, ISR-driven cue, acting convergently with FoxO rather than downstream of it.

studies.title: Transcriptional modulation of the PI3K/AKT/mTOR signaling pathway mediated by HPV16 E5, E6, and E7 oncogene expression in breast cancer.
studies.finding: In breast tumour tissue (48 of 92 patients with usable RNA), HPV16 oncogene expression was associated with higher PI3K and lower mTOR transcript levels. The design is correlational and measures mRNA only, so it does not show that the virus activates the mTOR pathway.

studies.finding: TBC1D7 is the third core subunit of the TSC1-TSC2 complex regulating Rheb/mTORC1.

studies.finding: Exome sequencing and linkage in families with autosomal dominant familial focal epilepsy with variable foci identified loss-of-function mutations in DEPDC5, a GATOR1 subunit, in 5 of 6 additional published large families and in roughly 12% (10/82) of smaller focal-epilepsy families. studies.finding: S6K1 triggers betaTRCP-mediated degradation of the tumour suppressor PDCD4 to promote translation.

studies.title: Rapamycin administration in humans blocks the contraction-induced increase in skeletal muscle protein synthesis
studies.finding: Rapamycin given before resistance exercise blocked the early (1–2 h) post-exercise rise in human muscle protein synthesis, which was about 40% in the control group. Rapamycin also blocked the rise in ERK1/2 phosphorylation and blunted MNK1, so the authors conclude that mTORC1 drives the response only in part. The study measured acute protein synthesis, not muscle growth.

studies.title: mTOR regulates the pro-tumorigenic senescence-associated secretory phenotype by promoting IL1A translation
studies.finding: Explained HOW rapamycin calms 'inflammaging'. Senescent cells spew inflammatory signals (the SASP) that damage surrounding tissue and even feed tumors. mTOR powers this by translating IL1A, the cytokine at the top of the cascade. Rapamycin selectively shuts it down - and blocked senescent cells from fueling prostate tumor growth in mice.

studies.title: AMPK phosphorylation of raptor mediates a metabolic checkpoint
studies.finding: Found a SECOND way the energy sensor AMPK shuts mTORC1 down. Besides acting through TSC2, AMPK directly phosphorylates Raptor - the core mTORC1 subunit - to halt growth when energy runs low. This 'metabolic checkpoint' is exactly the switch that drugs like metformin and exercise tap into.

studies.finding: SIN1 maintains rictor-mTOR integrity and confers mTORC2 Akt-Ser473 kinase activity and substrate specificity.

studies.title: mTOR inactivation governs adaptive survival to ribosome biogenesis deficiency
studies.finding: mTORC1 inhibition does not restore ribosome biogenesis but redistributes limited ribosomes away from highly-translated 5'TOP mRNAs toward survival-essential transcripts, defining a 'translational fitness' mechanism that lets cancer cells survive ribosome biogenesis deficiency.

studies.title: The translational landscape of mTOR signalling steers cancer initiation and metastasis
studies.finding: Showed WHY mTOR-driven translation matters for cancer: in prostate cancer, oncogenic mTOR selectively translates a specific set of pro-invasion mRNAs that drive metastasis. An ATP-competitive mTOR inhibitor (INK128) reversed that signature - an early preclinical rationale from mouse models and cell lines, not a clinical result.

studies.title: Active-site inhibitors of mTOR target rapamycin-resistant outputs of mTORC1 and mTORC2
studies.finding: The parallel discovery to Thoreen 2009 (same year), from the Shokat lab. Their TORKinibs (PP242, PP30) block mTOR's active site, hitting both complexes and shutting down cap-dependent translation that rapamycin misses. Together these two papers established a whole new drug class beyond rapamycin.

studies.title: Genetic dissection of the oncogenic mTOR pathway reveals druggable addiction to translational control via 4EBP-eIF4E
studies.finding: Genetic dissection shows the 4E-BP1-eIF4E axis mediates oncogenic mTOR signalling and is druggable.

studies.title: Synergistic role of TFEB/TFE3 and mTORC1 in kidney cystogenesis and tumorigenesis
studies.finding: Using kidney-specific mouse models that genetically uncouple mTORC1 activity from TFEB/TFE3 activity (Depdc5-KO, RagC-KO, and Flcn/RagC double-KO), the authors show mTORC1 hyperactivation -- not TFEB/TFE3 activation alone -- is the primary driver of kidney cystogenesis and tumorigenesis in Birt-Hogg-Dube and Tuberous Sclerosis Complex models. studies.title: A lysosome-to-nucleus signalling mechanism senses and regulates the lysosome via mTOR and TFEB
studies.finding: A lysosome-to-nucleus mechanism uses mTOR-dependent TFEB phosphorylation to sense lysosomal state.

studies.title: TFEB links autophagy to lysosomal biogenesis
studies.finding: Showed that TFEB drives a coordinated autophagy and lysosomal gene programme during starvation. In this paper TFEB was regulated by ERK2 phosphorylation; its control by mTORC1 at the lysosome was established in later work (SET2012).

studies.title: TFEB controls cellular lipid metabolism through a starvation-induced autoregulatory loop
studies.finding: The authors found that fasting switches on the TFEB gene in mouse liver, muscle and kidney, and that TFEB drives its own transcription by binding CLEAR sites in its promoter, an autoregulatory loop that starvation strengthens. studies.title: Late-life rapamycin treatment reverses age-related heart dysfunction
studies.finding: Striking evidence that in mice mTOR inhibition doesn't just SLOW aging - it can partly reverse an established age-related phenotype. Giving rapamycin to already-old (24-month) female mice for 3 months improved aged heart function, reversing or attenuating age-related cardiac changes, with RNA-seq changes suggesting anti-hypertrophic and anti-inflammatory effects. Started late, still worked.

studies.title: Mice fed rapamycin have an increase in lifespan associated with major changes in the liver transcriptome
studies.finding: Rapamycin-fed mice show extended lifespan with major changes in the liver transcriptome.

studies.title: Lifespan benefits for the combination of rapamycin plus acarbose and for captopril in genetically heterogeneous mice
studies.finding: NIA Interventions Testing Program C2017 cohort. studies.journal: J Gerontol A Biol Sci Med Sci
studies.finding: None of five popular longevity compounds had a statistically significant effect on lifespan. The paper explicitly states the ITP's mission is to publish all results, positive or negative - the exact registry model this Atlas should emulate.

studies.title: mTOR regulates the pro-tumorigenic senescence-associated secretory phenotype by promoting IL1A translation
studies.finding: Explained HOW rapamycin calms 'inflammaging'. Senescent cells spew inflammatory signals (the SASP) that damage surrounding tissue and even feed tumors. mTOR powers this by translating IL1A, the cytokine at the top of the cascade. Rapamycin selectively shuts it down - and blocked senescent cells from fueling prostate tumor growth in mice.

studies.finding: The paper that broke the simple 'metformin works through AMPK' story.
